title: Classic Eggs Benedict
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Melt the 60 g of butter in a small saucepan over low heat. In a separate small bowl, beat the egg yolks together with 10 ml lemon juice, 15 ml heavy cream, salt, and pepper.
Temper the egg mixture by adding a small spoonful of hot melted butter while whisking vigorously, repeating one spoonful at a time until all butter is incorporated to prevent curdling.
Pour the tempered hollandaise mixture back into the saucepan and cook on low heat while stirring constantly for 20–30 seconds until glossy, then remove from heat and set aside to thicken.
Fill a medium pot with 7-8 cm of water, add a tablespoon of vinegar, bring to a gentle simmer, and create soft movement in the water without letting it boil rapidly.
Crack an egg into a small cup, slide it gently into the simmering water, and poach for 3–5 minutes until the whites are set and the yolk remains soft, then remove with a slotted spoon.
Sear the 120 g of ham in a skillet over medium-high heat for 1 minute per side while the eggs are poaching.
Toast the English muffin halves, top each with ham and a poached egg, then generously drizzle with warm hollandaise sauce before serving.

title: Eggs Florentine
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Melt 60 g of butter in a small saucepan for the sauce. In a separate bowl, whisk the egg yolks with lime juice, 15 ml heavy cream, salt, and pepper.

Temper the egg yolks by adding hot melted butter one spoonful at a time while whisking continuously to avoid curdling, then pour the mixture back into the saucepan and warm gently over low heat for a few seconds before removing from heat.
Fill a pot with 7-8 cm of water, add vinegar, bring to a gentle simmer just below boiling point, and create a soft whirlpool with a spoon.
Crack an egg into a small cup, lower it into the center of the swirl, and cook for 3–4 minutes for a runny yolk before removing with a slotted spoon.

Melt 30 g of butter in a large skillet over low heat, pour in 60 ml heavy cream, simmer for a couple of minutes until slightly thick, then add 300 g baby spinach and cook for 2–3 minutes until wilted before seasoning with salt and pepper.
Toast and lightly butter the English muffin halves, layer generously with creamed spinach, place a poached egg on top, and finish with a rich layer of hollandaise sauce.

title: Classic American Buttermilk Pancakes
ingredients: 30 g butter, melted (plus extra for pan)
instructions: Heat a griddle or large non-stick skillet over medium heat (around 175°C) and lightly grease with melted butter.
Whisk together the dry ingredients in a large bowl, combining 250 g flour, 25 g sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
Pour in 480 ml buttermilk, beaten eggs, and 30 g melted butter, mixing just until the dry and wet ingredients come together without over-mixing the thick batter.
Ladle about 60 ml of batter per pancake onto the hot skillet, scatter blueberries or chocolate chips on top if desired, and cook until bubbles form on the surface.
Flip the pancakes once the edges look set and cook the second side until golden brown, then serve warm with maple syrup.

title: Classic French Bouillabaisse
ingredients: Fresh thyme and rosemary to taste
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Scale and clean the red snapper, then carefully remove the two fillets and set them aside. Place the fish carcass and head directly into a stockpot. Shell the shrimp and transfer only the shells to the pot with the fish bones.
Add fresh thyme, rosemary, black pepper, salt, and cover everything with water. Place over medium-high heat and simmer to create a rich, fragrant seafood broth.
Rinse and peel the vegetables as needed. Dice the yellow onions, slice the carrot, celery, leek, fennel, and bell pepper into thin strips, and finely mince the garlic cloves.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven. Start by sauteing the onions until translucent, then toss in the remaining sliced vegetables and cook until nicely browned.
Peel and dice the pumpkin (or potato) along with the fresh tomatoes. Add them into the pan with the sauteing vegetables and cook for another 10 minutes until soft.
Finely zest the lemon and squeeze out the fresh juice from the orange.

Cut the sea bass fillet into bite-sized pieces and add them to the vegetable mixture. Pour in the white wine, stir thoroughly, add the lemon zest and orange juice, then simmer until the alcohol completely evaporates.

Rinse the mussels under cold running water. Transfer them to a separate pot, pour in a little water with a splash of wine, and cook covered until all shells pop open. Remove most mussels from their shells, keeping a few intact for serving.

Strain the simmering fish and shrimp broth through a fine mesh sieve. Pour the strained broth into the cooked vegetable pan along with the shelled mussel meat, adjusting the liquid amount to your preferred soup density, then bring to a boil for 5 minutes.
Add the saffron threads to the boiling soup, blend everything with an immersion blender until completely smooth, and pass it through a sieve once more back into a clean pot.
Slice the remaining red snapper fillets. Drop the fish pieces, peeled shrimp, and scallops into the blended soup base, then cook gently until the seafood is perfectly done.
Serve the rich bouillabaisse piping hot, garnished with the reserved mussels in shells and accompanied by toasted baguette slices.

title: Classic Vichyssoise (Leek & Potato Soup)
ingredients: 350 g white part of leek, washed and sliced
Fresh chives or parsley, finely chopped (for garnish)
Salt and freshly ground white pepper to taste
instructions: Trim the dark green tops from the leeks, thoroughly rinse the white parts under cold water to remove any trapped dirt, and slice them finely into half-moons.
Melt the butter in a heavy-bottomed saucepan over low heat, add the sliced leeks with a generous pinch of salt, and sweat them slowly until completely soft without letting them brown.
Toss the peeled diced potatoes into the pot, pour in the hot chicken wing broth, and bring the liquid to a gentle boil.
Lower the heat to medium-low, cover the saucepan with a lid, and simmer for about 20 minutes until the potato cubes are soft enough to crush against the side of the pot with a spoon.

Remove the soup from heat and puree it with an immersion blender until completely smooth and velvety, then pass it through a fine mesh sieve into a clean bowl to eliminate any remaining fibrous leek bits.
Stir in the cream, season with salt and white pepper, then cover with plastic wrap pressed directly against the surface to prevent a skin from forming.
Chill the soup thoroughly in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, then ladle into chilled bowls and garnish with finely chopped fresh chives or parsley before serving cold.

title: Portuguese Fish Stew (Caldeirada de Peixe)
ingredients: 350 g potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes
450 g skinless white fish fillets (haddock or cod), cut into large chunks
A handful of fresh cilantro leaves, roughly chopped
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a heavy-bottomed Dutch oven or large casserole pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion, sliced red bell pepper, finely chopped garlic, chili flakes, and chopped cilantro stems, then cook for about 8 minutes until the vegetables soften.
Pour in the dry white wine to deglaze the pot, then add the saffron threads and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer and let the liquid reduce by half to concentrate the aromatic base.

Toss in the cherry tomatoes, cubed potatoes, and pour over the fish stock. Season with a light pinch of salt and black pepper, cover with a lid, and simmer over medium-low heat for 15–20 minutes until the potatoes are completely tender when tested with a fork.

Arrange the white fish chunks gently on top of the cooked potato layer, followed by the shrimp, pushing them slightly down into the hot broth. Cover the pot again and cook on low heat for 5–7 minutes until the fish flakes easily and the shrimp turn pink and opaque.

Remove the pot from heat, gently discard the bay leaves, adjust the seasoning with extra salt or pepper if needed, and scatter the roughly chopped fresh cilantro leaves over the stew before serving piping hot with crusty bread.

title: Classic Croque Monsieur & Croque Madame
ingredients: 170 g Gruyère or Emmental cheese, grated
4 large eggs (C0) for Croque Madame version
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Melt 60 g of butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat, whisk in 30 g of flour, and cook while stirring constantly for 3 minutes to form a light roux.

Gradually pour in 360 ml of milk while whisking vigorously to avoid lumps, simmer until the sauce thickens slightly, then season with salt, pepper, mustard, and a dash of nutmeg before removing from heat.
Preheat the oven to 220°C (425°F) and line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Spread a thin layer of béchamel sauce all the way to the edges on one side of all 8 bread slices.
Place 4 slices sauce-side up on the baking sheet, top each with ham, a handful of grated Gruyère, and a sprinkle of Parmesan, then cover with the remaining bread slices sauce-side up.
Scatter the remaining Gruyère and Parmesan cheese evenly over the tops of the sandwiches.
Bake at 220°C for 5–6 minutes until the cheese melts, then switch the oven to grill/broil mode for 2–4 minutes until the top is bubbly and golden brown.

To turn the Croque Monsieur into a Croque Madame, fry 4 eggs sunny-side up in a hot buttered skillet while the sandwiches are baking and place one fried egg on top of each hot sandwich before serving.

title: Classic Pasta alla Norma
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Wash the eggplants, cut them into small cubes, and spread them evenly over a parchment-lined baking sheet. Drizzle with 2 tablespoons of olive oil, season with ⅓ tsp of salt and ⅓ tsp of black pepper, then bake for 20 minutes until soft and golden.
Finely mince the garlic cloves and dice the fresh tomatoes into small pieces.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil, drop in the penne pasta, and cook until al dente for about 6–7 minutes after boiling.

Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat together with the minced garlic, chili flakes, and ⅓ tsp of salt. Pour in the canned pelati tomatoes, crush them slightly with a spoon, and cook for 5 minutes before tossing in the diced fresh tomatoes and chopped fresh basil sprigs.
Transfer the baked eggplant cubes and drained al dente pasta directly into the bubbling tomato sauce, stir everything well to coat the penne, and remove the skillet from heat.
Plate the pasta hot and generously shower each serving with grated Ricotta Salata cheese.

title: Classic Pasta Napoletana
ingredients: 220 g spaghetti, bucatini, or short pasta
1 tbsp olive oil or extra virgin olive oil (plus more for drizzling)
400 g canned tomatoes (whole, diced, or cherry tomatoes)
½ tsp fine salt (plus more to taste)
⅛ tsp freshly ground black pepper
1 handful fresh basil leaves, chopped or torn
3 tbsp freshly grated Parmesan cheese for serving
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat until shimmering, then add the finely chopped onion and cook for 5–6 minutes until soft and translucent.
Stir in the minced garlic and cook for about 2 minutes until fragrant without letting it brown.

Pour in the canned tomatoes, add the salt and black pepper, and stir well to combine. Simmer over medium heat for about 15 minutes until slightly reduced, stirring occasionally and gently crushing whole tomatoes with the back of a spoon if using them.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil around 5 minutes after starting the sauce, drop in the pasta, and cook per packet instructions until al dente. Reserve ½ cup of starchy pasta water, then drain the pasta.

Taste the finished tomato sauce and adjust salt and pepper to your liking. Add the drained pasta directly into the pan along with the fresh basil and toss vigorously to coat, splashing in a bit of reserved pasta water if needed to make it extra juicy.
Divide between plates, garnish with freshly grated Parmesan, extra torn basil leaves, a crack of black pepper, and a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil before serving immediately.

title: Classic Pasta alla Puttanesca
ingredients: ½ small bunch fresh parsley, finely chopped
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-low heat, add the finely chopped onion with a generous pinch of salt, and fry for 10 minutes until soft.
Add the crushed garlic and chili flakes, then cook for 1 additional minute until fragrant.
Stir the chopped tomatoes, anchovies, olives, and capers into the onion mixture, bring to a gentle simmer, and cook uncovered for 15 minutes before seasoning to taste.
Bring a large pan of salted water to a boil, cook the spaghetti according to packet instructions until al dente, then drain.
Toss the drained spaghetti directly into the pan with the bubbling sauce and chopped fresh parsley until evenly coated, then serve immediately.

title: Classic Chicken & Shrimp Pad Thai
ingredients: 225 g raw shrimp or chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: Cook the flat rice noodles in boiling water according to package instructions just until tender, drain immediately, and rinse under cold running water to stop the cooking process.
Whisk all the sauce ingredients together in a bowl until the sugar dissolves completely and set aside.
Heat 25 ml of oil in a large wok or deep skillet over medium-high heat, add the garlic, bell pepper, and chicken or shrimp, then stir-fry until the protein is cooked through.
Push the cooked ingredients to one side of the wok, pour the remaining oil into the cleared space, add the beaten eggs, and scramble quickly into small soft curds with a spatula.
Add the drained noodles, prepared sauce, bean sprouts, and half of the chopped peanuts into the wok, tossing everything vigorously over high heat to combine and heat through.
Transfer to plates and garnish with green onions, fresh cilantro, remaining chopped peanuts, and lime wedges before serving immediately.

title: Sweet and Sour Crispy Chicken
ingredients: 600 g boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into 2.5 cm cubes
2 bell peppers (1 red, 1 green), cut into large chunks
½ sweet onion, cut into large chunks
Cooked jasmine or white rice for serving
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
240 ml apple cider vinegar or rice vinegar
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C and line a baking dish with parchment paper.
Season the cubed chicken breasts with salt and black pepper, place them in a bag with 130 g cornstarch, and shake until every piece is evenly coated.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over high heat, dip the cornstarch-coated chicken pieces into the beaten eggs, and sear in batches for 1 minute per side until golden and crispy.
Transfer the seared chicken into the baking dish and bake at 200°C for 12–15 minutes until fully cooked through.
While the chicken bakes, saute the bell pepper chunks and onion in the same skillet over medium heat for 3 minutes until tender-crisp.
Whisk all the sauce ingredients together in a bowl, pour into the skillet with the vegetables, and simmer while stirring constantly until the sauce thickens and turns glossy.
Remove the chicken from the oven, pour the hot sauce and vegetables directly over the crispy chicken, toss to coat, and serve hot over steamed white rice.

title: Risotto Verde (Spinach Risotto)
ingredients: 400 g Carnaroli or Arborio risotto rice
1 medium yellow onion or 2 shallots, finely minced
1.2 liters hot vegetable or chicken stock
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Blanch the fresh baby spinach in a pot of boiling water for 30 seconds, transfer immediately to ice water, squeeze out excess moisture, and purée in a blender with 100 ml of warm stock until vibrant green and smooth.
Melt 25 g of butter in a heavy-bottomed saucepan over medium-low heat, add the minced onion, and sweat slowly for 5 minutes until soft and translucent without browning.
Add the risotto rice to the pan and toast for 2 minutes while stirring constantly until the grains become translucent at the edges and smell nutty.
Pour in the white wine and stir until it completely evaporates and the alcohol cooks off.
Begin adding the hot stock one ladleful at a time, stirring frequently and allowing the rice to absorb the liquid almost completely before adding the next ladle.
After about 15 minutes, when the rice is nearly al dente, stir in the smooth spinach purée and continue cooking for another 2–3 minutes.

Remove the pan from heat for the final mantecatura step, add the remaining 25 g butter, heavy cream, and grated Parmesan cheese, then cover with a lid and let rest for 2 minutes before beating vigorously with a wooden spoon until creamy.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve immediately on flat plates with extra grated Parmesan on the side.

title: Classic Risotto alla Parmigiana
ingredients: 1.6 liters low-sodium chicken or vegetable stock
½ medium yellow onion, finely diced
1 tbsp fresh parsley, finely chopped (for garnish)
Salt and freshly cracked black pepper to taste
instructions: Pour the stock into a saucepan and bring it to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then lower the heat to minimum so the liquid stays hot throughout the cooking process.

Melt 30 g of butter with 15 ml olive oil in a heavy Dutch oven or deep skillet over medium-low heat, add the finely diced onion with a pinch of salt, and sweat for 6–7 minutes until soft and translucent without browning.
Stir in the pressed garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the rice to the pot, increase to medium heat, and toast for 2–3 minutes while stirring constantly until the edges of the grains turn translucent.
Pour in the dry white wine to deglaze the pan, stirring continuously until the alcohol evaporates and the liquid is completely absorbed.

Add the hot stock one ladle at a time, stirring frequently and allowing the rice to absorb almost all the liquid before adding the next ladle, repeating this process for about 20 minutes until the rice is al dente.

Remove the pot from heat for the mantecatura step, stir in the remaining 30 g of butter and 50 g of freshly grated Parmesan, cover with a lid, and let rest for 2 minutes before beating gently until creamy.
Season with salt and freshly cracked black pepper, garnish with chopped parsley and extra grated Parmesan, then serve immediately on flat plates.

title: Fudgy Dark Chocolate Brownie
ingredients: 160 g eggs (C0 category, approx. 3 large eggs)
instructions: Melt the dark chocolate together with the 82.5% butter over a water bath or in short microwave bursts until fully combined. Whisk the cocoa powder directly into the hot chocolate-butter mixture to allow the cocoa flavor to bloom completely and stabilize the fat phase.

Whip the 160 g of eggs with the white sugar on high speed until a light, pale, and fluffy foam forms, similar to a classic sponge cake base. Gently fold the sifted wheat flour into this egg foam using a spatula to preserve maximum air volume.

Pour the warm chocolate mixture into the whipped egg base and gently combine using folding movements. Fold in the brown sugar last, making sure not to dissolve its crystals as these undissolved sugar grains will create the signature chewy and fudge texture during baking. Carefully stir in the optional chocolate callets, chopped nuts, and vanilla extract.

Transfer the batter into an 18x18 cm baking pan lined with parchment paper. Place the filled pan in the refrigerator for 10 minutes before baking to stabilize the texture, equalize humidity inside, and achieve maximum density.

Bake in a preheated oven at 160°C using conventional top and bottom heat for 30–40 minutes. The finished brownie must remain moderately moist in the center and medium in thickness, so avoid overbaking it into a dry sponge cake. Serve warm with a scoop of vanilla ice cream and salted caramel.

If your total egg mass exceeds 160 g (for example, 200 g), divide 200 by 160 and multiply the resulting coefficient by the weight of every other ingredient to perfectly maintain all technical proportions.

title: Classic Crêpes Suzette
ingredients: 30 ml vegetable oil (plus extra for frying)
instructions: Whisk together the eggs, vegetable oil, 30 g sugar, and a pinch of salt in a bowl, then sift in the flour and mix until smooth.
Pour in the milk gradually in small portions while whisking constantly until a thin, lump-free batter forms.
Heat a skillet over medium heat, grease lightly with vegetable oil, ladle in a portion of batter, tilt the pan to spread evenly, and fry each crêpe for 1 minute per side until light golden.
Rinse the orange, peel wide strips of zest taking care to avoid the bitter white pith, and squeeze out all the fresh juice.
Pour the orange juice, zest strips, and 30 g of sugar into a clean pan, bring to a simmer over medium heat, and allow the mixture to reduce slightly.
Fold the cooked crêpes into quarters to form triangles and lay them gently into the bubbling orange sauce.
Simmer the crêpes in the sauce for 1 minute per side until they soak up the citrus flavor.
Pour 45 ml of Cognac over the pan and carefully ignite with a match to flambé the dessert, allowing the flames to burn out naturally after a few seconds as the alcohol evaporates.
Remove from heat, transfer the warm crêpes to plates, drizzle with remaining orange sauce from the pan, and serve immediately with a scoop of vanilla ice cream if desired.

title: Unleavened Dough
instructions: Sift the flour into a large bowl, add salt, and mix well.
In a separate small bowl, lightly beat the egg with a fork.
Make a well in the center of the flour, then pour in the beaten egg and vegetable oil.
Stir the flour mixture with a fork to combine the ingredients slightly.
Pour the boiling water in a thin stream into the flour while stirring constantly and vigorously with a fork.
Continue stirring as the dough cools down; do not add extra water even if it appears dry at first.
Once the dough is warm and safe to touch, continue kneading it by hand inside the bowl, then transfer it to a work surface.
Knead until smooth, shape into a ball, cover with a towel, and let rest for 20 minutes.

title: Phyllo Dough
instructions: Combine all ingredients except the cornstarch in a bowl or stand mixer fitted with a dough hook attachment.
Knead until the dough becomes smooth, soft, and no longer sticks to your hands.
Slap the dough vigorously against the work surface several times for a few minutes to increase elasticity.
Wrap the dough tightly in plastic wrap and chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into portions, take 3 small pieces, dust the surface with cornstarch, and roll each piece into a small circle.
Generously dust each rolled circle with cornstarch and stack them directly on top of each other.
Roll all 3 layers simultaneously, constantly checking and adding cornstarch between layers to prevent them from sticking together.
Cover the rolled dough with a towel and let rest for a few minutes.
Continue rolling until each layer becomes paper-thin and translucent.
Repeat the process with the remaining dough, keeping finished sheets covered with a towel or plastic wrap at all times to prevent drying.

title: Choux Pastry (Eclairs / Choux / Paris-Brest)
instructions: Combine the water, milk, unsalted butter, salt, and sugar in a saucepan and bring to a boil over medium heat.
Remove the saucepan from heat and immediately add all the flour at once, whisking vigorously and constantly.
Return the saucepan to medium heat and cook the panade, stirring continuously with a wooden spoon for 1–2 minutes, until a thin white film forms on the bottom of the pan.
Transfer the cooked dough to a large bowl or a stand mixer fitted with a paddle attachment and allow it to cool slightly.
Optionally pass the eggs through a sieve, then slowly add them one by one while stirring on low speed.
Monitor the texture carefully: the dough should be glossy and smooth, falling off the spatula in a V-shape, without being too liquid or overly firm.

title: Puff Yeast Dough (Croissant Dough)
instructions: Set aside 100 g of softened butter and keep the remaining 250 g of butter cold in the refrigerator.
In a deep bowl or stand mixer bowl, combine the flour, 100 g softened butter, powdered sugar, milk powder, salt, and crumbled fresh yeast.
Pour in 230 ml of water and knead into an elastic, smooth dough that does not stick to hands.
Lightly flour a work surface and roll the dough out into a medium-thick rectangle.
Slice the 250 g cold butter into medium-thick slices and arrange them in a diamond pattern in the center of the dough.
Fold the free edges of the dough over the butter to enclose it completely.
Gently roll out the dough into a rectangle, ensuring the butter remains fully sealed inside.
Transfer to parchment paper and chill in the refrigerator for 1 hour (or freezer for 40 minutes).
Roll out the dough, fold it like a book, and chill for another hour; repeat this folding and chilling process at least 4 times.
Trim the outer edges after the final turn to allow the layers to expand properly during baking.

title: Puff Pastry (Pâte Feuilletée)
instructions: Sift 300 g of flour into a bowl and keep 250 g of butter in the refrigerator.
In a saucepan, melt 50 g of butter with 150 ml of water, 10 g salt, and a pinch of sugar over low heat.
Pour the melted butter and water mixture into the flour and knead into a soft dough ball.
Wrap the dough ball in plastic wrap and chill in the freezer for 40 minutes.
Make a cross-shaped incision on top of the chilled dough, unfold it, and roll into a rectangular sheet.
Place the remaining 200 g cold butter in the center and fold the edges over to form an envelope.
Roll out into a long rectangle, fold into thirds, and chill in the freezer for 40 minutes.
Repeat the rolling, folding, and chilling process 4 to 6 times before using.

title: Shortcrust Pastry (Pâte Brisée)
ingredients: 1 egg yolk + cold water (75 g combined weight)
instructions: Pour the flour onto a clean work surface and add the cold cubed butter.
Rub the butter into the flour quickly using your fingertips until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs.
Add the salt and the combined egg yolk and water mixture.
Gently mix with your fingertips until the dough comes together.
Perform the fraisage technique: smear the dough against the work surface twice with the palm of your hand to ensure complete homogeneity without melting the butter.
Shape into a flat disc, wrap tightly in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.

title: Fresh Egg Pasta Dough
ingredients: 2.5 ml (½ tsp) extra virgin olive oil
instructions: Mound the '00' flour on a clean work surface and create a wide well in the center.
Crack the room-temperature eggs into the well, then add the extra virgin olive oil and sea salt.
Using a fork, beat the eggs gently and gradually incorporate the flour from the inner rim of the well.
Once a shaggy dough forms, begin kneading by hand for 8–10 minutes until smooth, elastic, and springy.
Wrap the dough tightly in plastic wrap and let it rest at room temperature for at least 30 minutes before rolling.

title: Classic Opera Cake (Gâteau Opéra)
ingredients: 300 g whole eggs (approx. 6 large eggs C0)
35 g unsalted butter, melted and cooled
40 g Baileys liqueur (or additional heavy cream)
40 g dark chocolate (for sealing the bottom)
instructions: Joconde Sponge - Merengue & Eggs: Whisk 200 g egg whites with ¼ tsp salt until soft beer-like foam. Add 3 tbsp of sugar (from the 200 g total) and whip to stiff, glossy peaks. Do not over-whip. In a separate bowl, whip 300 g whole eggs with the remaining sugar on high speed for 4 minutes until pale and voluminous.

Joconde Sponge - Mixing & Baking: Mix almond flour with sifted all-purpose flour. Whisk into the whole egg mixture until smooth. Gently fold in the whipped egg whites in 3 additions using a spatula. Take 3 tbsp of batter, mix thoroughly with 35 g melted (and cooled) butter, then gently fold this back into the main batter. Divide between two 30x32 cm sheets lined with Teflon or parchment. Bake at 170°C for 12–15 minutes until light golden. Let cool, then cut out two 20x29 cm rectangles and assemble a third rectangle from the remaining sponge scraps.
Coffee Syrup: In a saucepan, combine 150 g water, 100 g sugar, and 5 g instant coffee. Bring to a boil until fully dissolved. Transfer to a measuring cup and let cool completely.

Chocolate Ganache Filling: Pour 150 g boiling heavy cream over 190 g chopped 54% dark chocolate. Let sit for 2 minutes, add 40 g Baileys, and blend with an immersion blender until smooth. Cover with plastic wrap in contact with the surface and chill until room temperature (soft and spreadable).

Coffee Buttercream Base: Boil 60 g water, 180 g sugar, and 5 g instant coffee to exactly 118°C. Meanwhile, whip 100 g egg yolks on high speed until pale. Slowly pour the hot 118°C coffee syrup into the whipping yolks in a thin stream. Continue whipping at high speed until the mixture cools completely to room temperature (crucial step).

Coffee Buttercream Assembly: Once the egg-coffee base is at room temperature, gradually add 340 g room-temperature butter 1 tablespoon at a time while continuously whipping until smooth, light, and silky.

Base Isolation: Melt 40 g dark chocolate. Brush a paper-thin layer onto the underside of the first sponge layer. Chill in the fridge until hard. Flip the sponge over onto parchment so the chocolate side is on the bottom.

Cake Assembly: Soak the bottom sponge with ⅓ of the coffee syrup. Spread half of the coffee buttercream in an even layer. Top with the middle sponge (made of scraps, fitted tight together), soak with ⅓ of syrup, and spread all of the chocolate ganache. Place the third sponge on top, soak with the remaining syrup, and spread the second half of the coffee buttercream. Smooth the top layer perfectly using an offset spatula. Chill in the fridge for at least 2 hours.

Glaze & Finishing: Melt 150 g of 70% dark chocolate with 150 g hot heavy cream until glossy. Let cool slightly to warm. Pour over the chilled cake and smooth quickly with a spatula. Chill until set. Trim the edges with a long, clean knife dipped in warm water and wiped dry before each cut. Slice into 12 equal portions and pipe the classic 'Opéra' signature on top using remaining chocolate ganache.

title: Crêpe Complète
instructions: Warm up your pan with a little olive oil.
Lay a crêpe in the pan, add a slice of ham cut in little pieces, crack your egg open and place it at the centre of your crêpe.
Add quickly a fourth of the emmental cheese around the egg yolk.
Fold in your pancake each side to make a square as per the recipe picture so as the egg white cannot get in direct contact with the pan. Wait until your egg is cooked.

title: Pasta alla Boscaiola
ingredients: 450 g rigatoni or penne or whatever
instructions: Pour hot water over the dried mushrooms to reconstitute them. Once reconstituted, squeeze out the liquid and set them aside.

Heat a large pan over medium heat and add 30 ml of olive oil to the pan. Brown the sausage and break it up with a wooden spoon. Once the sausage is cooked through, remove it to a plate tented with foil.

Turn the heat up a touch and add the remaining olive oil (30 ml) to the pan along with the mushrooms. Brown the mushrooms until they release their water and it evaporates (about 5 minutes). Once they release their water, toss in the reconstituted porcini mushrooms and cook for another 2 minutes, then season with a touch of salt.

Add the onions to the pan and cook until soft (about 4–5 minutes). Add the garlic and the rosemary and cook for 2 minutes longer or until golden. At this time, cook the pasta until 1 minute less than al dente.
Add the white wine to the pan with the onions and cook for 2–3 minutes or until the liquid reduces by about half. Return the sausage to the pan and add the tomatoes. Bring the sauce to a simmer.

Add the pasta to the pan and cook, stirring frequently, until it reaches a perfect al dente. Once it's al dente, remove the pan from the heat and add in the grated cheese and the parsley. If the sauce is too thick, add some of the reserved pasta water to thin it out. Taste test and adjust salt and pepper levels. Serve with more grated Parmigiano.

title: Pasta alla Nerano
instructions: To prepare Spaghetti alla Nerano, start by placing the zucchini on the heat: wash and trim them, then thinly slice them into rounds using a mandolin. Heat olive oil in a large frying pan, once the oil reaches 150°C, the ideal frying temperature, immerse the zucchini slices a few at a time to avoid lowering the oil temperature, cook for about 5-6 minutes, enough time to make them golden brown.

Once cooked, drain them using a skimmer and place them on a tray lined with paper towels to remove excess oil. As you cook the zucchini, season them with salt and sprinkle hand-torn basil leaves over them. Set the zucchini aside and bring a high-sided pot of salted water to a boil for cooking the spaghetti. Meanwhile, grate the Provolone del Monaco using a coarse grater. Then, cook the pasta until it is very "al dente" (around 6 minutes of cooking time).

Meanwhile, in a wide pan, heat 30 g of extra virgin olive oil, add the whole garlic cloves to infuse the flavor, then remove the garlic cloves with kitchen tongs, and pour in the previously fried zucchini.

Add a ladleful of pasta cooking water and quickly sauté the zucchini for a moment to soften them slightly and prevent them from becoming dry. After approximately 6 minutes of cooking the spaghetti, drain them directly into the pan with the sauce, making sure to save the cooking water.

Add a ladle of pasta cooking water, as needed, to continue cooking the spaghetti, stirring them like risotto: it will take about 3 minutes. Then turn off the heat. Pour in the grated Provolone del Monaco, stirring the spaghetti to melt it and create a creamy sauce.

Enhance the flavor further by adding hand-torn basil leaves and pour in another ladle of pasta cooking water. Stir well and once ready, sprinkle with freshly ground pepper. Serve your piping hot Spaghetti alla Nerano!

title: Japanese Stir-Fried Noodles(Yakisoba)
instructions: Heat 30 ml of neutral oil in a large wok or pan over medium heat. Add the noodle blocks and warm both sides until they loosen, using chopsticks to gently separate them. Transfer noodles to a plate.
Add the pork belly to the pan, season with black pepper, and stir-fry until no longer pink.
Add the onion and cook for 1–2 minutes until tender.
Add the carrot and cook for 1–2 minutes until it starts to soften.
Add the cabbage and shiitake mushrooms; cook until slightly softened.
Add the green onions and cook for 1 minute until wilted.
Return the noodles to the pan over the meat and vegetables. Pour the prepared sauce over everything and toss continuously until evenly coated and heated through.

title: Classic Pasta alla Gricia
ingredients: 225 g guanciale (cured pork jowl), in one piece
Fine sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
60 g finely grated Pecorino Romano cheese, plus extra for serving
instructions: Freeze guanciale for 15–30 minutes to firm up, then cut into 6 mm thick batons.

In a large skillet, heat olive oil over medium-low. Add guanciale and cook until crisp and golden, about 15 minutes. Transfer meat to a plate with a slotted spoon. Reduce heat to low, bloom 1 tsp freshly ground black pepper in the rendered fat for 1 minute, and remove skillet from heat.
Meanwhile, bring 2.8 L of lightly salted water to a boil in a pot. Add rigatoni and cook for 5 minutes (it will be very undercooked). Reserve 475 ml of starchy pasta water, then drain the pasta.

Pour the 475 ml of pasta water into the skillet and bring to a boil over high heat, swirling to emulsify with the fat. Add the rigatoni and cook, stirring constantly, until al dente and the sauce is thick and glossy, about 6 to 8 minutes; add a splash more pasta water if the skillet dries out. Fold in the cooked guanciale.

Remove from heat. Add half of the Pecorino Romano and toss rapidly until fully melted, then repeat with the remaining half. Adjust consistency with a little more pasta water if needed, season to taste, and serve immediately with extra cheese.

title: Classic Pasta all’Amatriciana
ingredients: 150 g guanciale, rind removed, cut into 1 cm slices then 0.5 cm strips
75 g finely grated Pecorino Romano cheese, plus extra for serving
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil for the pasta; salt lightly once boiling.

In a skillet over low heat, cook guanciale for 7–8 minutes until fat renders translucent and meat turns crispy. Deglaze with white wine, raise heat, and let evaporate completely. Transfer guanciale to a plate, leaving rendered fat in the skillet.
Add seeded chili and crushed tomatoes to the skillet fat. Simmer sauce over medium heat for 10 minutes; season with salt to taste. Discard chili pepper.
Meanwhile, cook spaghetti in the boiling water until al dente, reserve a splash of pasta water, and drain.
Add spaghetti and cooked guanciale to the skillet with sauce. Toss rapidly over medium heat to combine, adding a splash of pasta water if needed.
Remove from heat, fold in Pecorino Romano, toss well, and serve immediately with extra cheese.

title: Classic Spring Rolls
ingredients: 1 large carrot, cut into thin matchsticks
1 large red bell pepper, cut into matchsticks
12 large (22 cm) circular rice paper sheets
instructions: Boil the shrimp in a pot of water for 2 minutes until fully cooked. Drain, let cool for 5 minutes, peel the shells off, and slice each shrimp in half horizontally.
Submerge the rice vermicelli in boiled water for 5 to 8 minutes until softened. Drain, rinse under cold running water, and snip with kitchen scissors into shorter strands.
Set up a assembly area with a bowl of warm water, a lightly dampened chopping board, and all prepared ingredients placed nearby.

Dip a sheet of rice paper briefly in warm water to moisten and lay flat on the board. Lay a lettuce leaf near the bottom edge and layer a small amount of noodles, carrot, cucumber, bell pepper, and mint on top. Arrange 3 shrimp halves, pink side down, about 4 to 5 cm below the top edge of the sheet.

Lift the bottom edge of the rice paper over the vegetable filling, roll upward slightly, fold in both sides tightly, and finish rolling up toward the top edge. Repeat with remaining ingredients and serve with the dipping sauce.

title: Sopa Azteca (Tortilla Soup)
ingredients: 2 large dried pasilla chiles (or ancho chiles), stemmed and seeded
1 medium white or yellow onion, diced
800 g Roma tomatoes, diced (or canned diced tomatoes)
Fine sea salt and freshly cracked black pepper, to taste
Fried corn tortilla strips or chips
Chopped fresh cilantro, sour cream (or Mexican crema), lime wedges
instructions: Toast the chiles over an open gas flame or in a dry skillet for a few seconds per side until fragrant and blistered, then place them in a blender.

Heat the olive oil in a large stockpot over medium-high heat, sauté the onion for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and cook for another 1–2 minutes before transferring both to the blender with a slotted spoon.
Add the diced tomatoes and 240 ml of the stock to the blender, then purée until completely smooth.
Pour the blended mixture back into the stockpot, add the remaining stock, oregano, and epazote, bring to a simmer, and cook uncovered over medium-low heat for 10 minutes.
Prep your desired add-ins while the soup simmers, placing a handful of tortilla strips and shredded chicken into individual serving bowls.
Season the simmering broth with salt and pepper to taste.
Ladle the hot broth into the serving bowls over the toppings, add avocado, cheese, cilantro, sour cream, and lime, and serve immediately.
